chunks: Ali, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Al-Zayyat, from Abdullah ibn Aban Al-Zayyat—who held a distinguished position with Al-Rida عليه السلام—who said:
I said to Al-Rida عليه السلام, "Pray to Allah for me and for my household." So he said, "Am I not already doing so? By Allah, your deeds are surely presented to me every day and night."
He said: I regarded that as tremendous, so he said to me, "Do you not read the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic?"
And say: Work; so Allah will see your deeds, and His Messenger, and the believers.
He said, "He is, by Allah, Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام."

key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنُونَ: The believers, interpreted here as referring specifically to Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام
key_terms.عَلِيُّ بْنُ أَبِي طَالِبٍ: Imam Ali عليه السلام, identified in this narration as the intended referent of the believer
key_terms.كِتَابَ اللَّهِ: The Book of Allah, meaning the Qur'an

ai.seo_question: Do the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and the Imams عليهم السلام see the deeds of people according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that deeds are presented regularly to the Imam عليه السلام, and it connects that reality to the Qur'anic statement that Allah, His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and the believers see people's deeds. The Imam عليه السلام identifies the "believer" in the verse as Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام, indicating a special station of awareness and authority.
